name: i32-accum
notes: Wrapping 32-bit accumulate of `i & 65535`. The mask is what stops LLVM's scalar-evolution pass closing the loop into n*(n-1)/2; verified by the N-vs-2N scale test. Loop form is idiomatic per language: `for i in 0..n` (Rust), `for(;;)` (JS), `range()` (Python), `while` (VL — VL has no range-for). JS needs `|0` per step for int32 semantics; Python folds mod-2^32 once at the end, which is exact because the body is pure addition. 2N stays inside i32 (2e9 < 2^31), which caps how large N can be while keeping the scale test valid. opt.vl is a HAND-OPTIMIZED 4-accumulator 4x unroll, kept separate; it is not a recommendation.

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 58ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 12% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.rustVectorised: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT — rustc -O AUTO-VECTORISES this loop and no meta note said so. Confirmed by disassembling `main::main`: the hot loop is SSE2 packed integer arithmetic (paddd/pand, 4-wide, 4 accumulator chains, unrolled 16x per branch). rustc's default target is baseline x86-64, so this is 128-bit SSE2; `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` widens it further. The Rust:VL multiple on this benchmark is therefore mostly SIMD WIDTH, not scalar codegen quality — VL emits no SIMD. Report it as such.
audit.rustVectorisedNumbers: rustc -O 57.4ms; rustc -O -C target-cpu=native 27.7ms (AVX2, 8-wide); VL 307.7ms. Rust:VL is 5.4x at baseline and 11.1x at native — the SCALAR codegen gap is ~1.4x.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
